swept: A node scan of all 32 wines, every sale and every staged description, for the engine's words() and sentences() (sale two sentences, 15 to 45 words; description 104 to 110), the dish link rule (every printed dish name against the wine's derived firstPickIds, secondFor and offeredWith, and every tier word beside it), the step against the record, BANNED_WORDS, superlatives (best, finest, greatest, most, top, legendary, iconic, world class, every -est word, than any, than anyone), hedges, prices, questions, allergens, dashes, American spellings from the engine's own list, provenance, living names (the engine's list, printed names exempt), every proper name and year against the hay and the house, the eight word run against the s20 and the opening on the printed name. Found: superlatives (Viña Cubillo the youngest red; Insignia beef at its grandest, sale and description; Caymus Special Selection at its fullest in the sale and the winery's top Cabernet in the description) and one American spelling (Rubicon, percent), all fixed; the other hits were plain facts (the only appellation in Italy for a single estate, one of the first Super Tuscans, Silver Oak makes only Cabernet), left as they stand. Insignia's apparent eight word run was the hyphen in its s20's Cabernet-led; by the engine's count it is seven.
